To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

urinary P excretion was constant until the STTD P requirement for maximum growth was reached and then increased linearly with STTD P intakes, and the FMC increased with dietary STTD P intake until the STTD requirement was reached and then plateaued.

urinary P excretion was constant at low levels of P intake, but increased linearly at high levels of P intake and was highly predictable from dietary STTD P intake; urinary Ca excretion decreased with increasing levels of dietary Ca intake and reached a plateau at high levels of intake, and was highly predictable with dietary Ca intake; femur mineral content increased with increasing levels of P intake but plateaued at high levels of STTD P, and the femur mineral content was highly predictable from STTD P

urinary P excretion is constant until a plateau is reached at STTD P intakes above the requirement, urinary Ca excretion is constant, FMC increases with STTD P and then reaches a plateau, and P and Ca excretions in urine are only moderately predictable from the dietary STPD P and Ca intake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model for predicting P excretion in urine of pigs based on the STTD P, Ca, and P intake.
the quantitative relationship between dietary STTD P, Ca, and their retention and urinary excretion in growing swine fed corn-soybeans diets.
the quantitative relationship between the dietary STTDP and Ca intakes and their absorption, retention, excretion, and accumulation in bones in growing pigs fed diets based on corn and soybean meal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dietary STTD Ca and P intakes were highly predictable for P and Ca excretions and retention in growing pigs.
the dietary STTDP and Ca intakes are the major factors that determine the P and Ca excretions in urine, but other factors, such as FMC, also play a role in determining the urinary P excretions.
dietary STTD P intake above the requirement is used for growth and bone deposition and excreted in excess in the urine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dietary P requirement for growing pigs could be estimated by the FMC.
dietary STTD P is used for growth and bone mineral deposition, and when excess P is available, it is excreted in the urine, but when excess Ca is available, it will be deposited in the bones.
STTD P intake is a useful parameter in predicting P excretion in urine and P absorption and retention in growing pigs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
P excretion in urine can be reduced by feeding diets with a high STTD P content.
the urinary P excreted by growing pigs fed diets with STTD P above the requirement is not a constant but increases linearly with STTD P intakes.
the STTD P requirement is 4.59 g of STTD P per day and the requirement is not met by feeding diets with STTD P intakes below 4.59g/d.
